rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources served with a notice to quit or non-renewal
rules.requirement: Any landlord or foreclosing owner who plans to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in Boston must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources. The notice must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to Quit or the notice of lease non-renewal or expiration. The landlord or foreclosing owner must also send the City a copy of the Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the Office of Housing Stability. Per the city page, this is done through the online portal, together with tenant contact information. The requirement cannot be waived, and lease terms that purport to waive it are void. The Office of Fair Housing and Equity investigates violations and the Inspectional Services Department enforces them: a warning for the first offense and $300 per day for second and later offenses. Failure to submit to the portal may result in a fine of up to $300 per day. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources served with the Notice to Quit or non-renewal; copy to the Office of Housing Stability; 1st offense warning, then $300/day; portal non-submission fine up to $300/day; non-waivable; eviction not halted

coverage.summary: Applies to all landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in Boston. The only exempt properties are residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and in non-profit facilities whose primary purpose is short-term substance-abuse treatment.
coverage.other_conditions: Exempt: residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse.

rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
rules.effective_date_note: The FAQ says the ordinance was passed by the City in October 2020 (exact day not stated) and that 'The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.'
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
rules.review_note: This is a notice and tenant-rights ordinance, not a just-cause list. The documents state no allowed eviction causes or relocation assistance for Boston. The ordinance text itself is not in the documents (D013 only links to it). The section number comes from the enforcement table in both official sources ('Sec. 10-11.7') and should be confirmed against the codified ordinance. As state context, G.L. c. 186, § 31 separately requires a state form with nonpayment notices to quit. HSNA is complementary to it and applies to all terminations and non-renewals.
rules.source_notes: D014 (official tenant FAQ) and D013 (official city page) describe the same ordinance. D013 says the notice 'should be delivered' with the notice to quit, while D014 says it 'must be delivered'. The mandatory reading is consistent with the enforcement schedule. D013 adds the online portal submission and the portal fine.

also_supported_by.quoted_span:
The Housing Stability Notification Act requires
ALL LANDLORDS
planning to end a tenancy agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.
Failure to submit this information may result in a fine up to $300 per day.
The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.

In the event that your landlord serves you with a Notice to Quit or Notice of Lease
Non-renewal or expiration, you should also receive the Notice of Tenants’ Rights
and Resources at the same time.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND-funded and inclusionary housing)
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-record ban; no consideration of non-conviction arrests, relieved convictions, juvenile records or convictions over 5 years old; no use of credit score

unverifiable_exemptions: Whether the housing provider received DND funding or land
Whether the unit is an income-restricted unit created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy
coverage.summary: Applies only to housing providers with DND funding or land, or with BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units. It is also applied to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program. It is not a citywide rule for all landlords.
coverage.other_conditions: Federal or state law imposing a conflicting criminal-history requirement preempts the policy.

rules.exemptions: Arrest and conviction limits do not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others, and do not apply to current criminal behavior. Conflicting federal or state criminal-history requirements preempt the policy.
rules.effective_date_note: The document is dated February 2017 but states no effective date.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)
citation_aliases: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.quoted_span:
Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or 
land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development 
Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions.
rules.review_note: This is an administrative policy that funded providers agree to, not a citywide ordinance. Several provisions are phrased as 'strongly encouraged' or 'should'. In_force status is inferred because no repeal or sunset is shown. The BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy is a separate policy that defines covered units, so it is not a citation alias.
rules.source_notes: The credit-screening and eviction-consideration provisions are part of the same policy and are folded into this record.

also_supported_by.quoted_span: d) A conviction more than 5 years old.
a) The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing

rules.title: H.3744, Boston rent stabilization home-rule petition (not enacted)
rules.requirement: Home-rule petition, approved by the mayor and city council, asking the Legislature to authorize the City of Boston to implement rent stabilization. The bill text is not in the documents, so no cap, formula or coverage is stated. On 9/9/2024 the bill accompanied a study order (H5035) and was not enacted in the 193rd General Court (2023-2024). No Boston rent cap is in force under this measure.

coverage.summary: Coverage unknown; the bill text is not in the documents.

rules.effective_date_note: Never enacted. The bill accompanied study order H5035 on 9/9/2024, and the 2023-2024 session has ended.
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
rules.review_note: Only the bill history page is available, not the bill text. As state context, G.L. c. 40P bars local rent control, which is why legislative authorization was sought. The statewide Initiative Petition 25-21 was also barred from the 2026 ballot.
rules.source_notes: H5035 is the study order the bill accompanied, not an alternate citation for this bill.

rules.title: H.3744, Boston tenant eviction protections home-rule petition (not enacted)
rules.requirement: The same home-rule petition also asked the Legislature to authorize the City of Boston to implement tenant eviction protections. The bill text is not in the documents, so no causes, notice or relocation terms are stated. On 9/9/2024 the bill accompanied a study order (H5035) and was not enacted in the 193rd General Court.

coverage.summary: Coverage unknown; the bill text is not in the documents.

rules.effective_date_note: Never enacted. The bill accompanied study order H5035 on 9/9/2024, and the 2023-2024 session has ended.
rules.quoted_span: that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
rules.review_note: The eviction-protection content is known only from the bill title and description. It is kept separate from the in-force HSNA notice ordinance because a failed measure is never merged into an enacted law.

dropped_candidates.reason: General overview page of local, state and federal fair housing law. It names no Boston ordinance or code section, so the rental-assistance protection cannot be tied to a specific local law. It may restate the state source-of-income bar (G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10)), which is already captured at state level. Listed under known_gaps.

known_gaps.law: Boston local fair housing ordinance enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission (rental assistance / source-of-income protection)
known_gaps.reason: The official page (D012) says Boston bars discrimination based on rental assistance and that the commission enforces local fair housing law. The ordinance is not named and its text is not in the documents, so no rule is created.
